Arrange on parchment-lined trays with space between pieces. Refrigerate promptly at ≤40°F until cooking. Keep raw meatballs covered and segregated from ready-to-eat foods.

For service, brown meatballs evenly in batches in a lightly oiled pan or on a hot plancha. Avoid crowding. Transfer to the prepared albondigas sauce and finish cooking gently until the center reaches the applicable safe cooking endpoint.
Hold and serve according to the restaurant's approved hot-holding procedure. Do not partially cook and chill unless a validated cooling and reheating process is in place.

PRODUCTION TARGET: Approximately 7,507 g mixture; portion 150 meatballs at 50 g each (30 orders × 5 meatballs). Actual yield will vary with bowl and handling loss; weigh finished mix and portion to 50 g rather than relying on theoretical count.
MEAT RATIO: 3,720 g beef PSMO tenderloin trim + 2,480 g in-house ground pork shoulder = 6,200 g total meat, 60/40 by meat weight. Tenderloin trim is lean; pork shoulder fat level will affect final texture. Evaluate a cooked test portion before forming the full batch. COOKING: Brown in batches, then finish gently in the albondigas sauce until fully cooked. Confirm the applicable safe internal temperature with a calibrated thermometer and the restaurant's approved food-safety plan. Do not infer cooking time without meatball size, equipment, and batch conditions.
HOLDING: Keep raw mixture ≤40°F; minimize time out of refrigeration. Use separate equipment and sanitation controls for raw meat. Refrigerate promptly and follow the restaurant's validated cooling, reheating, and hot-holding procedures. Transfer to a heavy-bottomed pot. Heat gently over medium-low heat, stirring and scraping the bottom frequently to prevent scorching or separation.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook only long enough to marry the flavors and reach a uniform service consistency. Do not hard-boil; coconut milk can separate and the sauce can scorch.
Taste and assess balance, salt, acidity, sweetness, spice, and viscosity. Any adjustment should be documented as a revision to the standardized 1:1:1 formula.

For service, reheat only the quantity needed using the approved reheating procedure. Stir frequently and maintain the restaurant's approved hot-holding temperature. Portion 180 g sauce per order.

storage: Refrigerated components; finish and hold per approved plan
plating:
PRODUCTION TARGET: 33 portions at 180 g each = 5,940 g total finished sauce. 30 orders require 5,400 g; the additional 540 g provides approximately 10% reserve. Formula is 1:1:1 by weight: 1,980 g house tomato sauce + 1,980 g house mole + 1,980 g coconut milk.

MOLE COMPONENT: Use the established house mole recipe without modification. Allergen status cannot be determined without reviewing that recipe and its supplier labels.
PROCESS: Heat gently, stir frequently, avoid hard boiling and scorching. Coconut milk may separate under aggressive heat. Validate final seasoning and service viscosity with a test batch before locking the recipe.
FOOD SAFETY: Follow approved cooling, refrigeration, reheating, and hot-holding procedures. Refrigerate at ≤40°F. This recipe does not establish a validated shelf life; use the shortest applicable shelf life among its components and the restaurant's food-safety plan.

name: Black Cherry, Pepita & Black Lime Mole

ingredients.name: Dried chile blend
ingredients.note: 90 g ancho + 70 g pasilla + 60 g guajillo + 12 g morita; stemmed and seeded. Hot water for soaking/blending is process water, added as needed.

ingredients.name: Certified gluten-free masa harina
ingredients.note: Corn masa; no wheat flour or bread

ingredients.name: Black lime powder
ingredients.note: Food-grade dried black lime, finely ground

steps.name: Sort dried chiles; remove stems and seeds. Toast briefly in a dry pan or on a plancha over medium heat until fragrant and pliable. Do not blacken.
Cover toasted chiles with hot water and steep 20 minutes until fully pliable. Drain; discard soaking liquid if bitter.
Toast pepitas until fragrant and lightly golden. Toast sesame separately. Toast cacao nibs briefly until aromatic and masa harina until lightly nutty. Do not scorch.
Char tomatoes, onion, and garlic on a plancha, under a broiler, or in a hot oven until softened with dark blistered spots. Avoid heavy carbonization. Roast or sear plantain until golden and soft.
Warm neutral oil in a heavy pot. Add oregano, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, allspice, and clove; bloom 20–30 seconds until fragrant. Do not burn.

Blend softened chiles with roasted vegetables, plantain, cherries, pepitas, sesame, cacao nibs, masa harina, tamarind, coffee, vinegar, black lime powder, bloomed spices, initial salt, and enough hot water to move the blender. Work in batches until very smooth.
Pass through a fine chinois for a refined texture. Transfer to the pot. Add remaining water gradually, scraping blender clean, until thick but pourable.
Simmer gently 25–35 minutes, stirring frequently and scraping the bottom. Masa and seeds settle and scorch readily. Add water as needed to maintain a smooth, spoonable consistency.

Taste and adjust salt, vinegar, tamarind, and black lime carefully. Target savory dried chile and toasted pepita first, dark cherry acidity next, gentle smoke and cacao depth, with a subtle black-lime finish. It should not taste sweet, coffee-forward, or dessert-like.
Weigh finished mole and record actual yield. Cool rapidly in shallow pans using the approved cooling procedure; refrigerate at ≤40°F.

yieldText: Approx. 2.4–2.6 kg finished; weigh actual yield
plating:
BATCH TARGET: 1 US gallon (3.785 L) finished mole, measured after simmering and final texture adjustment. Formula is a 1.7× scale-up of the prior estimated 2.4–2.6 kg batch; actual finished volume depends on solids, reduction, and water additions. The multiplier is a starting production estimate, not a guaranteed volumetric yield.
PROCESS WATER: Use hot water as needed for chile soaking, blending, and texture. Add gradually. Measure finished volume after simmering; adjust texture with hot water if below 1 gallon, or reduce gently if above 1 gallon. Record actual batch weight and volume for future scaling.
APPLICATION: Albondigas Sauce requires 1,980 g mole for 30 orders plus 10% reserve. Weigh actual finished mole and reserve required amount.
GLUTEN-FREE: Use certified gluten-free masa harina and verify labels for dried chiles, cherries, tamarind, cacao, coffee, vinegar, and spices. Prevent cross-contact. Contains sesame and pumpkin seeds; declare sesame and verify supplier allergen statements.
PROCESS CONTROL: Toast chiles only until fragrant and pliable; scorched chiles become bitter. Toast seeds separately. Char vegetables without excessive carbonization. Blend very smooth. Simmer gently and stir frequently because masa and seeds settle and scorch. Hot water is process water, not a fixed formula ingredient.
FINISHING TARGET: Savory chile and toasted pepita first, dark cherry acidity, gentle smoke/cacao, subtle black lime. Not sweet, coffee-forward, or dessert-like. Test in finished Albondigas sauce before final seasoning.
FOOD SAFETY: Rapidly cool using the restaurant's approved cooling procedure and refrigerate at ≤40°F. This recipe does not establish a validated shelf life; use the shortest applicable validated shelf life in the food-safety plan.
SPICE FORMULA: All four dried chiles and every spice/seasoning are listed as individual ingredients in the expanded one-gallon ingredient list.

name: D.O.P. San Marzano Tomato Sauce

ingredients.name: D.O.P. San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes
ingredients.note: 2 standard #10 cans; assumed 2,977 g net weight each; verify actual can label

ingredients.name: Basil
ingredients.note: Whole leaves or torn; add near end

steps.name: Open and inspect both D.O.P. San Marzano #10 cans. Confirm the D.O.P. mark and record supplier lot details. Verify actual net weight on the cans; formula assumes 2,977 g per can.
Crush tomatoes by hand or pass through a food mill to the desired texture. Reserve all packing juice.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or steam-jacketed kettle, warm olive oil over medium-low heat. Add diced onion and sweat slowly until soft and translucent, without browning.
Add sliced garlic and crushed red pepper, if using. Cook gently 1–2 minutes until fragrant; do not brown the garlic.
Add crushed tomatoes and all packing juice. Add oregano and initial kosher salt. Stir to combine.

Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered over low heat, stirring regularly and scraping the bottom, until the raw tomato edge is gone and the sauce reaches a cohesive, lightly reduced consistency. Expect approximately 60–90 minutes depending on kettle geometry, heat, and tomato solids.
Add basil during the final 10 minutes. Remove basil stems or large leaves if used whole.
Taste and adjust salt only after reduction. Keep the sauce rustic and spoonable; do not reduce to a dense pizza sauce. Weigh finished sauce and record actual yield.
For advance prep, transfer to shallow pans or approved containers and cool rapidly under the restaurant's approved cooling procedure. Refrigerate at ≤40°F.

portion: Use 1,980 g in 30-order Albondigas sauce batch
plating:
BATCH BASIS: Scaled from the original formula for two standard #10 cans. A standard #10 can is assumed to contain 6 lb 9 oz (2,977 g) net weight; two cans = 5,954 g tomatoes. Check the actual label and adjust all other ingredients proportionally if net weight differs.
FORMULA: 5,954 g D.O.P. San Marzano tomatoes; 298 g EVOO; 595 g yellow onion; 60 g garlic; 60 g kosher salt (initial amount; adjust after reduction); 36 g fresh basil; 4.8 g dried oregano; 2.4 g crushed red pepper (optional).
YIELD: Finished yield depends on tomato solids and reduction; weigh the cooled finished sauce. Use 1,980 g for the 30-order Albondigas sauce batch. This batch should yield ample reserve, but do not rely on an estimated yield for production allocation.
STYLE: Rustic, clean tomato flavor; onion and garlic should support rather than dominate. Keep reduction moderate so the sauce blends smoothly at 1:1:1 with mole and coconut milk.
QUALITY CONTROL: Verify D.O.P. designation on packaging and retain lot details. Taste after reduction before final salt adjustment. If can net weight differs from 2,977 g, scale the entire formula by actual total tomato weight ÷ 5,954 g.
FOOD SAFETY: Cool rapidly using the restaurant's approved cooling procedure, refrigerate at ≤40°F, and use the shortest applicable validated shelf life in the restaurant's food-safety plan. This recipe does not establish a validated shelf life or shelf stability.

name: Duck Breast Prosciutto — Dry-Cured

ingredients.name: Duck breast
ingredients.note: skin on, trimmed; Reference batch weight; weigh each breast after trimming

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.note: 2.5% of duck breast weight; development starting point

ingredients.name: Brown sugar
ingredients.note: 0.8% of duck breast weight; balances cure

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: finely grated; 0.3%; optional; maintain strict sanitation

ingredients.name: Cure #2
ingredients.note: Do not dose from this sheet. Use only if included in the approved validated process, and calculate strictly from the exact manufacturer's label and applicable regulations

steps.name: Use fresh, sound duck breasts from an approved supplier. Keep refrigerated at 41°F / 5°C or below during receiving, trimming and cure preparation. Record raw weight of each breast.
Trim loose connective tissue and any damaged areas. Keep skin intact if desired for the finished presentation; do not score deeply into the meat.

Weigh salt and dry aromatics as percentages of the actual meat weight. Mix thoroughly and coat all surfaces evenly. Cure #2 is intentionally not assigned a quantity here: use only under a written, validated HACCP process and exact product label directions. Do not substitute Cure #1 or generic pink salt.

Place breasts in a nonreactive food-safe container or vacuum bag as specified by the approved process. Label each piece with lot, weight, cure date and operator. Keep at 34–38°F / 1–3°C during the curing stage unless the validated plan specifies otherwise.

Cure duration, turning schedule, rinse/wipe procedure and post-cure handling must follow the establishment's validated process. Do not use a fixed number of days from this development sheet as a safety endpoint.

After curing, prepare for drying exactly as specified in the approved HACCP plan. Use a calibrated curing chamber with continuously monitored and recorded temperature and relative humidity; prevent cross-contamination and ensure adequate airflow without surface case-hardening.

Do not release product based only on elapsed time, appearance or percentage weight loss. Verify the validated critical limits and finished-product criteria (including water activity where required) and document approval before service.
Once released, slice paper-thin across the grain. For the scallop dish, proposed use is 10–15 g per order, wrapped around scallops immediately before searing; validate slice size and cook behavior.

yieldText: 1 kg raw duck breast; weigh finished
storage: Curing chamber; release only under approved HACCP plan
plating:
CRITICAL FOOD SAFETY / HACCP:
This is a formulation starting point, NOT a validated ready-to-eat charcuterie process. Dry-cured duck is a time/temperature-controlled, reduced-moisture meat process with pathogen hazards. Do not produce or serve under this sheet alone.
Before production, have the process reviewed and approved by the establishment's qualified food-safety authority/regulatory authority. Establish product-specific critical limits for cure formulation, curing temperature/time, drying temperature/RH/airflow, endpoint (including aw), monitoring, corrective actions, packaging and shelf life.
Do not vacuum-package or otherwise oxygen-restrict the finished product unless that packaging step is specifically included in the validated process. Keep lot traceability and curing logs.

CURE #2 REFERENCE: the common manufacturer label rate for Cure #2 is 0.25% of meat weight (2.5 g per kg). Your sheet intentionally leaves it blank until the HACCP plan sets it. Most health departments require a HACCP plan and variance for in-house dry curing; confirm with yours before serving.

steps.name: Sort tomatoes; discard any moldy, fermented, or damaged fruit. Wash thoroughly under running potable water. Remove cores and any bruised areas; cut large tomatoes into quarters. Weigh 5,954 g after washing and before trimming only if your production standard defines the batch that way; record actual usable weight.
In a heavy-bottomed pot or steam-jacketed kettle, warm olive oil over medium-low heat. Add diced onion and sweat slowly until soft and translucent, without browning.
Add sliced garlic and optional crushed red pepper. Cook gently 1–2 minutes until fragrant; do not brown.
Add prepared tomatoes and their accumulated juices. Add oregano and approximately 80% of the initial salt. Stir to combine.

Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered over low heat, stirring and scraping the bottom regularly, until tomatoes collapse completely and excess water cooks off. Expect approximately 75–120 minutes depending on variety, ripeness, pot geometry, and water content.
Add basil during the final 10 minutes. Remove basil stems or large leaves if used whole.

Pass the cooked sauce through a food mill using a medium plate to remove skins and seeds while retaining body. If a more rustic texture is desired, crush by hand and leave skins/seeds in; use one method consistently for each batch.

Return milled sauce to the pot if needed and reduce gently to a cohesive, spoonable consistency. Taste and adjust salt after reduction. Keep it brighter and looser than a dense pizza sauce. Weigh finished sauce and record actual yield.
For advance preparation, transfer to shallow pans or approved containers and cool rapidly under the restaurant's approved cooling procedure. Refrigerate at ≤40°F.

yieldText: Approx. 3.8–4.6 kg finished; weigh actual yield
portion: Use 1,980 g in 30-order Albondigas sauce batch
plating:
BATCH BASIS: 5,954 g whole fresh farm heirloom tomatoes, matching the tomato starting weight used for the two-can D.O.P. San Marzano version. Select ripe, sound tomatoes with good flavor; mixed heirloom varieties are acceptable. Record whether the batch weight is taken before or after trimming and keep that standard consistent.
FORMULA: 5,954 g fresh heirloom tomatoes; 298 g EVOO; 595 g yellow onion; 60 g garlic; 60 g kosher salt as an initial amount (start with approximately 80%, then adjust after reduction); 36 g fresh basil; 4.8 g dried oregano; 2.4 g crushed red pepper optional.
YIELD: Do not assume equal finished yield to canned tomatoes. Fresh tomatoes vary widely in water content and trim loss. Expected finished yield is approximately 3.8–4.6 kg, but weigh actual yield. Albondigas Sauce production requires 1,980 g tomato sauce for 30 orders plus 10% reserve; weigh and reserve that amount after finishing.
METHOD / TEXTURE: Wash, core, and quarter. Sweat onion, add garlic, then tomatoes and aromatics. Simmer uncovered until collapsed and excess water has cooked off. Pass through a medium food mill to remove skins and seeds, then reduce to a rustic, spoonable consistency. For a deliberately rustic sauce with skins/seeds retained, crush by hand instead; choose one method and standardize it.
QUALITY CONTROL: Taste the raw tomatoes before production; sweetness, acidity, and water content vary by farm and cultivar. Adjust final salt only after reduction. If fruit is notably acidic, do not automatically add sugar; evaluate the finished sauce in the 1:1:1 mole/coconut blend first. Keep the finished sauce bright and spoonable.
FOOD SAFETY: Wash produce before cutting. Cool rapidly using the restaurant's approved cooling procedure, refrigerate at ≤40°F, and use the shortest applicable validated shelf life in the restaurant's food-safety plan. This recipe does not establish a validated shelf life.

steps.name: If frozen, thaw foie gras ends and pieces under refrigeration. Keep cold until ready to cook.
Cut foie gras into evenly sized pieces. Place in a cool pan and heat gently over medium-low heat, stirring as fat begins to render.
